skill.name: global-conventions
skill.description: Helps AI coding tools follow shared development conventions for project organization, version control, configuration, reviews, testing, feature flags, changelogs, and contribution workflows.
skill.summary: Apply shared development conventions for structure, reviews, configuration, testing, and release documentation.
skill.author: DevanB

remediation.suggestion: Move the referenced conventions content into the skill package and link to a local file without parent-directory traversal.

content.value_statement: Teams often lose time when project structure, commits, reviews, and configuration practices differ between contributors. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a shared checklist for consistent development conventions.
actual_capabilities: Directs agents to apply project organization and directory conventions.
Guides commit messages, branch choices, and pull request practices.
Covers environment variable and configuration documentation workflows.
Supports review, testing, changelog, and release note consistency.
Advises on feature flags, dependencies, and contribution guidelines.
limitations: The skill delegates detailed rules to a linked conventions document.
It does not execute scripts or inspect repositories by itself.
It does not replace project-specific policies, legal review, or security approval.
The referenced conventions file must be available to the agent.

use_cases.title: Align Pull Request Practices
use_cases.description: Use the skill to plan branches, commits, tests, review notes, and documentation before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Maintain Contribution Consistency
use_cases.description: Apply shared expectations for changelogs, setup notes, dependencies, and contribution guidance across repeated community changes.

use_cases.title: Guide Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Ask an AI coding agent to check structure, configuration, testing, and release notes against the same conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Project Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current task against the global conventions. Focus on file placement, documentation needs, and testing expectations before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pull request plan that follows our global conventions. Include branch naming, commit style, review notes, tests, and documentation updates.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Workflow Consistency
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this repository for convention drift. Compare structure, configuration handling, changelog habits, and review process against the global conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Process Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Help decide whether this unfinished feature should use a feature flag or a long-lived branch. Explain the tradeoffs using the global conventions.

output_examples.input: I am adding a new configuration file for a service.
output: Place configuration with related service documentation.
Document required environment variables in setup notes.
Add review and test notes before opening the pull request.

output_examples.input: I need a pull request checklist for a feature branch.
output: Confirm branch naming follows team practice.
Summarize commits with clear user-facing intent.
List tests, documentation updates, and changelog impact.

output_examples.input: Should this unfinished feature stay on a long-lived branch?
output_examples.output: The skill would compare the feature flag option against branch lifetime, review visibility, release timing, and team coordination.

best_practices: Use the conventions before starting repository organization or pull request work.
Keep the referenced standards document available and current.
Ask for explicit testing and documentation checks before final review.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill as a substitute for missing project policies.
Do not rely on it when the referenced conventions file is unavailable.
Do not let convention guidance override security or compliance requirements.

faq.question: What does this skill help standardize?
faq.answer: It helps standardize project structure, version control, configuration, reviews, tests, feature flags, changelogs, and contribution practices.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it modify files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance that an agent can apply during normal coding and documentation workflows.

faq.question: Does it include the full conventions text?
faq.answer: No. The skill points to a separate conventions document, so the package should include that content before publication.

faq.question: Is it useful for pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers branch choices, commit messages, pull request preparation, tests, documentation, and review expectations.

faq.question: Can it replace team review?
faq.answer: No. It supports consistent preparation, but reviewers must still check correctness, security, and project fit.
